run.e: From Middle English rennen, from Old English rinnan.

s.d: the act of running; traveling on foot at a fast pace
move fast by using one's feet, with one foot off the ground at any given time
x: Don't run, you'll be out of breath

s.d: direct or control; projects, businesses, etc.

x: The river runs through the valley

s.d: To manage or be in charge of.
